You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 1. The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and [STANDARD] labels

The note says clauses marked [STANDARD] are "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to review only [OPEN] items. Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN]. **We should not accept this.**

- The Seller applied these labels itself. I have nothing showing the Buyer agreed to any of these positions. Several of them are among the most Buyer-adverse terms in the package, including the knowledge bar, uncapped limitations scope, Riverlark and Bluefen.
- The note also says the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." I have no record of that. **Please confirm with the deal team whether anything was actually agreed** in the term sheet, heads of terms or prior correspondence. Unless something was, every item below remains open.
- Our cover response should say expressly that labelling a clause [STANDARD] does not mean the Buyer accepts it, and that all positions remain subject to our mark-up.

I have reviewed everything on that basis.

---

## 2. The limitation and disclosure package (the structural problem)

Each of these clauses could look market-ish on its own. **Taken together, they would largely empty the warranties of value.**

### 2.1 General disclosure of the data room and public records (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
- Disclosing everything in the data room and public registers puts the burden on the Buyer to find the problems. Combined with clause 8.3, almost any warranty claim is defeated.
- The data room is fixed at **22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026, so the record is about six weeks stale.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **fair, specific disclosure** in the Disclosure Letter qualifies the warranties. It must give enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter, and be made against the specific warranty affected.
  - Delete general disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers. At most, allow public registers searched on a specified date.
  - Supplementary disclosure must not qualify warranties repeated at Completion unless the Buyer consents. If a new matter is material, the Buyer gets a termination right.
- Note that most specific disclosures (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) are **disclosures of unresolved problems**. They should be dealt with through conditions, completion deliverables, price deductions and specific indemnities. They should not be "disclosed away."

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- This clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge attributed to advisers, which is very broad.
- **Push back:** Delete it. The preferred position is an express statement that warranties are not qualified by Buyer knowledge or investigation. The fallback is to limit the bar to *actual* knowledge of named individuals of matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter.

### 2.3 "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13) and limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- Read literally, these would apply the 20% cap, the 18-month period, the basket and the knowledge bar to:
  - specific indemnities (including Ironquay)
  - tax claims
  - debt-free/cash-free and completion adjustments
  - leakage
  - covenant breaches
  - title
  - potentially **fraud**
- Non-reliance applied to "all Claims" is also aimed at Australian Consumer Law s 18 misleading conduct claims.
- **Push back:** Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. Expressly carve out:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment or misstatement, by the Seller *or the Company's management*
  - Fundamental Warranties
  - Tax Warranties and the Tax Indemnity
  - specific indemnities
  - price adjustment and completion payment obligations
  - leakage
  - breach of pre-Completion covenants

  Non-reliance must be subject to a fraud carve-out and should not cover statements in the Disclosure Letter or written replies to DD requests.

### 2.4 Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit
- "Administrative simplicity" does not justify capping title at AUD 4.8m when we are paying AUD 24m for 100% of the shares.
- **Push back:**
  - Fundamental Warranties are capped at **100% of the purchase price**, with no de minimis or basket.
  - The claim period runs for the full limitation period. In NSW that is 6 years for contract claims and 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed (*Limitation Act 1969* (NSW)). Consider executing as a deed.

### 2.5 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- They are not settled. **Push back:**
  - A **stand-alone tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, including employment taxes (see bonuses below).
  - Capped at the purchase price.
  - Claim period of at least the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, commonly around 5–7 years.
  - Outside the basket and de minimis.
  - IP warranties should be treated as at least "enhanced," given Ironquay.

### 2.6 Cap, de minimis, basket and 18 months (cl 12.1–12.3)
- These are within market range for general warranties, so this is the place to make concessions if needed. Suggested asks:
  - **tipping basket** (recover from the first dollar once AUD 250k is exceeded) rather than recovery of only the excess
  - de minimis of around AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated
  - general cap of 30–50% if no W&I insurance is in place
  - 18–24 months is acceptable for general warranties
- If W&I insurance is being considered, the Seller's cap and retention could be adjusted around it. Note, though, that **known issues (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006) will be excluded from a W&I policy.** That is another reason they need specific protection from the Seller.

---

## 3. Specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2): HIGH
- Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m, roughly **30% of FY26 revenue**. It has a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3).
- The Seller confirms that no final consent has been obtained and the conditions are not shown as satisfied.
- The Seller's proposal has two weaknesses:
  1. It offers only "reasonable endeavours."
  2. It treats the condition as satisfied once *any* written consent is delivered, even if the consent is conditional or comes with adverse amendments, and even if the cl 11.3 conditions remain outstanding.
- **Push back:**
  - Condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer: an **unconditional** written consent from Bluefen in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, with evidence.
  - No variation to pricing, term or termination rights unless the Buyer approves.
  - The Seller must use **best or all reasonable endeavours**, and the Buyer participates in communications with Bluefen.
  - A long-stop date and a walk right.
  - Consider a warranty or indemnity, or price retention, if Bluefen terminates or materially varies terms within 12 months after Completion.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3): HIGH
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the facility has a change-control clause (8.1). **Completion itself may trigger a default or acceleration.**
- The Seller offers a release "following Completion." That is inconsistent with a **debt-free/cash-free** deal and would leave the Company owing the debt with security still in place.
- **Push back:**
  - Riverlark is repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price** under a payout letter, as a line item in the funds flow, and treated as Debt.
  - Completion deliverables:
    - an executed payout letter stating the exact payout figure as at Completion
    - deeds of release covering all security and guarantees
    - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a short fixed period
    - return of any title documents
  - A Riverlark change-control waiver if anything remains in place at signing.

### 3.3 DD-005 completion bonuses (funds flow; DL 5): HIGH
- The Seller says the AUD 420,000 in bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. **The Company is the employer**, so the Company bears:
  - the bonus payments
  - PAYG withholding
  - superannuation, if the bonuses form part of ordinary time earnings
  - NSW payroll tax
  - workers' compensation and other on-costs

  The disclosure itself confirms that the on-costs are not addressed. Post-Completion, the Buyer would effectively pay for these.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses plus all on-costs as **Transaction Costs/Debt**, deducted from the price.
  - Pay them through Company payroll at Completion from funds the Seller provides, or deduct and itemise them in the funds flow.
  - Add a specific indemnity outside the caps for any bonus, retention, change-of-control or similar entitlements, and related taxes, not captured.
  - Seek the full list of transaction-related employee entitlements, including any that crystallise on the continued-employment condition after Completion.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4): HIGH
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- On those facts, **the Company may not own IP that it uses.** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the debt but not the real risk:
  - no ownership
  - infringement claims
  - injunctions
  - remediation or re-development costs
  - customer claims
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion: evidence that every SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds, and an **executed confirmatory assignment** from Ironquay, with moral rights consents where relevant. Make this a CP or a completion deliverable.
  - If it is not delivered: retain or escrow an appropriate amount.
  - A specific indemnity covering all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or being unable to use, the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general limitations and be capped at no less than the purchase price or a negotiated high amount, with a long claim period.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6): HIGH
- A download link to around 1,240 personal information records was sent to an unintended external address. As at 22 September the following were unknown:
  - whether anyone accessed the file
  - the scope of the data
  - whether notification is required
- Under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must reasonably and expeditiously assess it, generally within 30 days. **That window may already have passed**, so non-compliance with the assessment obligation is itself a risk. Other possible exposures include:
  - OAIC regulatory action and penalties
  - notification and remediation costs
  - customer contract claims
  - individual claims
- "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation and has no evidence behind it.
- **Push back:**
  - Immediate updated disclosure: the incident date, the investigation report, access logs and link-expiry evidence, and the outcome of the NDB assessment and any notifications made.
  - Confirm whether contractual notification duties to customers were triggered.
  - A specific indemnity outside the caps and basket for all Losses arising from the incident: regulatory, notification, forensic, customer and third-party.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
  - A privacy/data warranty repeated at Completion.

### 3.6 Supplier renewals (DL 8): MEDIUM, needs facts
- Three *related* renewals of AUD 110,000 each total AUD 330,000. The Disclosure Letter says they should be read together for timing and scope, and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Calling them "ordinary-course operating costs" does not answer those points.
- **Concern:** the renewals may have been split to stay below a conduct-of-business or board-approval threshold. They may also be unbudgeted commitments or prepayments that reduce cash or count as leakage.
- **Ask:**
  - dates of entry (pre- or post-signing / locked-box date)
  - approvals obtained
  - term and termination rights
  - whether prepaid or accrued
  - whether related parties are involved

  If they were entered into after the relevant date without consent, treat them as a covenant breach or debt-like item. Aggregate related transactions in the conduct-of-business thresholds going forward.

### 3.7 Title (DL 10): MEDIUM
- A share register (DD-012) is the Seller's own record and is not enough on its own.
- **Push back:**
  - Fundamental title warranty covering: legal and beneficial ownership of 100% of the issued shares; fully paid; free of Encumbrances; no options, convertibles, ESOP or other rights to shares.
  - Treated as in 2.4.
  - We should verify independently: ASIC current and historical extract, constitution, share certificates, allotment and transfer history, and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.

### 3.8 Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9): MEDIUM/LOW, verify
- The Seller's reading is that the lease requires notification only and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. **We should not rely on that reading.** We need to read the actual clauses in DD-007 and DD-009 for deemed-assignment or change-in-control wording, including control of the tenant or a change in its shareholding.
- If confirmed: make the lease notification a completion deliverable or covenant, and add a warranty that no material contract is triggered by the transaction except those listed.

### 3.9 Funds flow: MEDIUM
- "Reflects the agreed price mechanics" cannot be verified and appears to leave out the Riverlark payout and the bonuses.
- **Push back:** Require a full itemised funds flow and completion statement showing:
  - Debt (including Riverlark)
  - Transaction Costs (including bonuses, on-costs and adviser fees borne by the Company)
  - Cash
  - working capital mechanics
  - any retention or escrow

  The Buyer should approve it, with a post-Completion true-up.

### 3.10 Disclosure Letter cl 1.4 (no admission)
- This is acceptable only if the SPA states that the Disclosure Letter cannot expand Seller limitations, create new exclusions, or qualify indemnities, Fundamental Warranties or Tax Warranties.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [STANDARD] labels / efficiency note | Treat as agreed; review [OPEN] only | Reject; all open unless deal team confirms prior agreement | Threshold |
| 2 | Scope of limitations / non-reliance | Apply to all Claims | General Warranty Claims only; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, fundamentals, price, leakage, covenants | High |
| 3 | General disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Fair specific disclosure only; no Completion bring-down disclosure without consent | High |
| 4 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual + constructive + advisers | Delete; fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters | High |
| 5 | Fundamental warranties | 20% cap / 18 months | 100% cap / full limitation period; consider deed | High |
| 6 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Unconditional consent satisfactory to Buyer + cl 11.3 satisfied as CP; best endeavours; walk right | High |
| 7 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Repaid from price at Completion; payout letter, releases, PPSR discharges as deliverables | High |
| 8 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | "Matter for Seller," excluded from funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Costs incl. payroll tax/super/PAYG; indemnity | High |
| 9 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment proof + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad IP indemnity outside caps; retention fallback | High |
| 10 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Full update and NDB assessment status; specific indemnity outside caps; pre-Completion covenant | High |
| 11 | Tax | Under general regime | Stand-alone tax indemnity, price cap, ATO-period-based time limit | High |
| 12 | Supplier renewals | Ordinary course | Facts on timing, approvals, terminability; treat as breach/debt-like if appropriate; aggregate in thresholds | Medium |
| 13 | Title | Share register | Fundamental warranty + independent ASIC/PPSR verification | Medium |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify clause wording; notification as deliverable | Medium/Low |
| 15 | Funds flow | "Reflects agreed mechanics" | Full itemised, Buyer-approved funds flow | Medium |
| 16 | Cap / basket / de minimis / 18 months | 20% / 250k excess / 25k / 18m | Tipping basket, lower de minimis, higher cap if no W&I; tradeable | Lower (concession area) |

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Confirm with the deal team whether any of these positions were previously agreed.
2. Issue an RFI to the Seller covering:
   - Bluefen consent status
   - the Riverlark payout figure
   - Ironquay payment and assignment
   - the DD-006 investigation and NDB assessment
   - details of the supplier renewals
   - bonus on-costs
   - an updated data room after 22 September
3. Prepare the mark-up on the positions above, leading with the limitation and disclosure structure and the five High items under specific issues.

This analysis is based only on the Seller's summary and the Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the underlying DD documents or the full SPA text, so the clause-specific points (Bluefen 11.2/11.3, Riverlark 8.1/9.2, the lease and Mossvale) should be checked against the source documents.
